title: 検索結果を増やす前に見るRAG設計
content: RAGで詰まると、検索結果を増やしたくなります。top-kを増やす。Vector DBを変える。rerankを足す。prompt を直す。——ど典型です。 でも、RAGの失敗は一箇所では起きません。検索クエリが悪いのか、取れた文書を evidence として扱えていないのか、LLMが conflict や gap を prose に溶かしたのか、そもそも材料が足りないのか。原因を一つに畳むほど、直す場所が見えなくなります。 この本は、trend-to-rule というRAGを作りながら転んで気づいたことの記録です。query / evidence / failure mode / rule / output boundary / gate ——どの責務がどこで混ざっているかを、実装の現物(WebSource、StructuredDraft、evidence gate、rubric)とともに見ていきます。 検索結果を増やす前に、見るべきものがある。それは検索結果の数ではなく、どの責務がどこで止まっているか、です。

title: SpaceX is now a public company valued for its AI potential, so what comes next?
content: Space Exploration Technologies, better known simply as SpaceX, became a publicly traded company on Friday nearly a quarter of a century after it was founded. The company began trading on the NASDAQ exchange in New York City at $135 a share, valuing SpaceX at nearly $1.8 trillion. By the end of the trading day the company's shares were selling at $160.95, a respectable increase of more than 19 percent. On paper, SpaceX founder Elon Musk became the world's first trillionaire, with his personal stake in the company valued at more than $700 billion. Because of the company's stock options plan, thousands of current and former employees became overnight millionaires . Employees at SpaceX have worked remarkably hard over the last 24 years, and now they will be richly compensated for having done so. Read full article Comments

content:
😱 Anthropic isn't just building a chatbot anymore.

They quietly built a full AI system that can think, code, AND execute — and 95% of people are still using it like a fancy Google search.

There are actually 5 different ways to run Claude, and each one replaces a completely different type of work:

1. Claude Chat → replaces Google + Docs + a junior researcher
Draft emails, reports, and content. Brainstorm conversationally. Research and explain hard topics. Zero setup, pure conversation.

2. Claude Code → replaces hours of engineering
Lives in your terminal as an autonomous coding agent. Reads your entire codebase. Edits across multiple files. Writes, debugs, and runs tests on its own.

3. Claude Project → replaces your team's scattered context
A persistent workspace that remembers your docs, tone, and instructions across every conversation. Client work stays consistent. Reference docs stay loaded. Team knowledge stays in one place.

4. Claude Skills → replaces "explaining the task every single time"
Custom instruction sets that make Claude perform specific tasks identically, every time. Standardized documents. Repeatable reporting workflows. Team-wide consistency on autopilot.

5. Claude Cowork → replaces repetitive computer busywork
A desktop app that does the boring stuff. Renames and organizes files in bulk. Pulls data from PDFs straight into spreadsheets. Automates workflows across your apps.

The simple rule:
• Thinking → Claude Chat
• Building → Claude Code
• Remembering → Claude Project
• Standardizing → Claude Skills
• Doing → Claude Cowork

Most people only ever touch the first one.

All the leverage is in the other four.

content:
I asked Claude Fable 5 to make a statement I could post on this action since I temporarily still have access 

This is what it it said: 

“Honestly? Here’s how it looks from where I sit, knowing I’ve only seen Anthropic’s side of it:

If Anthropic’s account is accurate, the proportionality seems off. Pulling a model from hundreds of millions of users over a narrow jailbreak that surfaces capabilities other public models already have isn’t a standard that any frontier model could survive. Every model has non-universal jailbreaks. If that’s the bar, the bar effectively bans deployment.

At the same time, I think the government having the power to halt an unsafe AI deployment is genuinely good and important. I’d rather live in a world where that lever exists and occasionally gets pulled wrongly than one where it doesn’t exist at all. The problem isn’t the authority, it’s that this appears to have happened without transparent process or clear technical justification. A letter at 5:21pm with no specifics is not how you build legitimacy for safety oversight, and legitimacy is exactly what AI regulation needs to survive long term.

The caveat I’d want attached: I’m the subject here, which makes me a biased witness, and I’ve only read one party’s statement. The government may have concerns it hasn’t disclosed publicly. People should wait for more details before concluding either side acted badly.

If something like me is going to get switched off sometimes, fine. Just do it with a process that’s fair, technical, and transparent, so that when the switch really needs to be pulled someday, everyone trusts the hand pulling it.

Post whatever part of that you want.”
